data_objects.name: physiological_samples
data_objects.meaning: A multi-file logical table of participant-partitioned, session-labeled physiological samples. Each row carries a time coordinate and aligned EDA, HR, temperature, and BVP channel values.

data_objects.name: survey_responses
data_objects.meaning: Participant survey-response records with reported start and end times, a recorded duration and date, a coded stress level, and contextual 0/1-coded fields.

variables.name: session
variables.meaning: Session identifier composed of the participant code, an underscore, and an integer timestamp-like suffix.

variables.name: real_time
variables.meaning: Numeric absolute-looking time coordinate for a physiological sample; sampled within-session values advance in 0.25 increments.

variables.name: eda
variables.meaning: Electrodermal-activity signal channel aligned to the row time coordinate.

variables.name: hr
variables.meaning: Heart-rate signal channel aligned to the row time coordinate.

variables.name: temp
variables.meaning: Temperature signal channel aligned to the row time coordinate.

variables.name: bvp
variables.meaning: Blood-volume-pulse waveform channel aligned to the row time coordinate.

variables.name: ID
variables.meaning: Participant identifier; its values correspond to subject filename identifiers and session prefixes.

variables.name: Start time
variables.meaning: Recorded interval start timestamp encoded as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS without a stated timezone.

variables.name: End time
variables.meaning: Recorded interval end timestamp encoded as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS without a stated timezone.

variables.name: Duration
variables.meaning: Recorded interval duration encoded as HH:MM:SS.

variables.name: Date
variables.meaning: Separate calendar-date field encoded as YYYY-MM-DD; its semantic basis is not stated.

variables.name: Stress level
variables.meaning: Coded stress-level response with observed values 0, 1, and 2; scale anchors and direction are not supplied.

variables.name: COVID related
variables.meaning: Coded field for COVID-related context; only value 0 is observed.

variables.name: Treating a COVID patient

structure.description: The physiological object is partitioned into one named file per participant. In the representative files, the filename participant code also prefixes every sampled session identifier.

Physiological rows form a participant-to-session-to-sample hierarchy. Within representative sessions, real_time advances by 0.25 seconds and all four signal columns share that row coordinate; their native channel rates are not established.

The sampled BG file contains overlapping sessions whose rows are interleaved and can share the same real_time value. Consequently real_time alone is not a row key; session plus real_time is the natural composite locator, though global uniqueness was not exhaustively verified.
Each survey row is an interval-level response for one participant. Participant IDs repeat, and all 15 observed survey IDs correspond to the 15 subject-file identifiers.

The survey table has no explicit session or response identifier. Participant ID supports a participant-level relationship to the physiological files, but the files do not establish a one-to-one survey-row-to-sensor-session mapping.
Participant plus Start time plus End time is not unique in the survey table: two such interval tuples recur with different contextual codes.

uncertainties: The public CSVs provide no data dictionary or unit metadata. Physical units for eda, hr, temp, and bvp are therefore left unknown.
The epoch/origin and timezone of real_time are not declared, and the survey timestamps are timezone-naive, so temporal alignment between the two objects is not established.
The source does not state whether signal values are raw, resampled, interpolated, or device-derived. A shared 0.25-second row grid does not establish each channel's native cadence.
The meanings, direction, and anchors of Stress level codes 0/1/2 and the truth/selection mapping of the contextual 0/1 fields are not documented.
The Date field differs from the calendar date in Start time for some survey rows, but the role of this separate date is not explained.
No blank values were observed in the compact survey table or bounded signal samples; undocumented numeric sentinel values cannot be ruled out.
annotation_notes: Physical inventory contains 15 subject CSV files and one survey_results.csv file.

Representative content inspection was bounded to subject_15_combined.csv, subject_83_combined.csv, subject_BG_combined.csv, and the compact survey_results.csv; other subject files contribute only to the physical inventory.
The annotation is task-independent and uses only the permitted public artifacts and routed scientific-modality guidance.
